patch.value: An option's operand was read as the program in two places, once failing open and once failing closed

Two review findings on the same pull request, both confirmed by executing the branch before changing anything, and both about the same mistake made in opposite directions: an option's operand was not consumed, so the word after a flag was read as something it is not.

The first is a fail-open in the shebang interpreter check. Skipping only dash-prefixed words after env read the operand of -u and -C as the interpreter, and read a NAME=value assignment as the interpreter under -S. Measured: #!/usr/bin/env -S FOO=bar bash, #!/usr/bin/env -S -C /work bash and #!/usr/bin/env -u FOO bash all answered not-shell, so a genuine bash script drops out of the scan entirely and a publish inside it is never audited. Fixed by parsing env's grammar rather than its punctuation: skip dash options, consume the operand of the ones taking a separated one, skip any NAME=value assignments, then take what remains. -S is deliberately excluded from the operand set because in a shebang it splits the rest of the line rather than taking one operand, so consuming a word after it would swallow the interpreter it exists to introduce.

The second is a false failure in the spawning-wrapper detection. The prefix walk skipped a dash option but left its operand in place, so env -u parallel npm --version set the spawning-wrapper flag from parallel, which is -u's operand rather than a command, and npm --version was audited as a possible publish. Measured on both env -u parallel npm --version and env -C xargs npm ci. For a gate that blocks releases across twenty repositories a false failure costs an outage, not a missed publish. Fixed with a per-prefix map of options that consume the next word, keyed by the prefix because the same spelling differs by command: sudo -u takes a user, env -u takes a variable name, nice -n takes a number.

The second fix changed an existing guarantee rather than only adding to it, which is worth recording. commandCandidates deliberately offered every reading of a wrapper-led command on the stated grounds that nothing enumerated which options take a value. That is now partly false, so a known option's operand no longer starts a reading. The test now asserts both halves rather than quietly dropping the old one: a known option's operand is not a reading, and an unknown option's value still is, with an end-to-end assertion that a publish behind an unknown option is still found.

Applying the first fix twice surfaced a separate problem tracked elsewhere: the two test files covering this auditor share 55 identical test titles with the same bodies, so a fix to one leaves the other failing in a way that reads as a regression.
Parsed env's grammar for the interpreter check, and added a per-prefix map of options that consume the next word for the wrapper walk, so an operand is never read as the program in either place.
A genuine shell script behind env options is scanned, and an option's operand is never mistaken for a spawning wrapper.
env -u FOO bash answered not-shell so the file left the scan entirely, and env -u parallel npm --version was audited as a possible publish.
